background_subtraction_window — VIDEOSTREAM window op

• Data kinds: video → video

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.background_subtraction_window(video, window: 'int' = 5, threshold: 'float' = 0.1) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import videostream; videostream.background_subtraction_window(video, window: 'int' = 5, threshold: 'float' = 0.1) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsvideostream.get("background_subtraction_window"))

Usage

Causal window-median background → per-frame 0/1 foreground masks (T, H, W) (video).

For each frame t, the per-pixel median of the most recent window frames (max(0, t-window+1) .. t, including that frame itself) is taken as the background bg, and |frame_t - bg| > threshold is set to 1, everything else to 0. Future frames are not looked at (causal), so at the start the window is shorter by the number of frames that are missing.

• video: a (T, H, W) array, or a list of 2-D frames of the same shape and same dtype. uint8/uint16 is mapped to [0, 1] by the dtype maximum, float is clipped to [0, 1] as is. Colour (T, H, W, C) is not accepted. NaN/Inf gives ValueError.

• window: int from 1 to 4096 (not bool). With 1 the background = the frame itself, so all pixels are 0. For an even number of frames the median is the mean of the 2 middle values.

• threshold: in intensity units of [0, 1] (for uint8, converted as /255).

• Returns: (T, H, W) float64 of 0 / 1.

• Failure: ValueError (shape, dtype, range, non-finite).

Slowly moving objects melt into the background within window frames; in that case use running_gaussian_foreground (selective update) or exponential_foreground. If you need the background itself, temporal_median_window.
